body.x: VANAM (CEO Soo Deok Han) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Established in early 2022, VANAM, an early-stage startup, uses its proprietary thin film growth technology to develop next-generation semiconductor thin film materials and components. This technology forms from an exclusive process that precisely controls the thin film's thickness, composition, and other characteristics, creating high-quality, highly uniform thin films. VANAM's technological prowess received appreciation for its significant potential. It ensures the quality of thin films and opens up endless possibilities for using materials and devices previously inaccessible to traditional manufacturing technologies and methods. In line with this, VANAM is constructing a micro foundry in downtown Seoul, focusing on deposition processes and expanding its manufacturing capabilities.

At this year's CES, VANAM showcased energy-sensitive semiconductor thin film materials and components essential for applications such as fire detectors and protective circuits. The company actively promoted these products to global electronics companies, particularly battery and IoT device manufacturers. By emphasizing safety, a common trend in both the international industry and consumer technology sectors, VANAM aims to seek sales opportunities in the global market.

In response, VANAM pointed to the commercialization of its first project, the energy-sensitive semiconductor thin film 'VM1.' High-quality semiconductor thin films produced through environmentally friendly vacuum deposition produce VM1. It is the first in energy-sensitive semiconductors to adopt a thin film form.

According to the company, VM1 can react very sensitively to heat and electrical energy due to its form, significantly enhancing the detection performance of safety systems. It is a key component that could replace bulkier semiconductor components like thermistors and varistors commonly used before.

body.cap: VANAM representatives, including CEO Soo Deok Han (pictured right), posed with their products. │ Photo - AVING News

body.x: A VANAM representative stated, "As safety-related trends strengthen in industries and consumer technology worldwide, our product, which boasts specialized responsiveness, can be an attractive alternative." The representative expressed the company's goal of commercializing materials made thinner through environmentally friendly processes that have yet to appear in the market. They emphasized their commitment to collaborating and exchanging ideas with participating companies offering diverse services to explore potential applications and continue ongoing research and development.

In addition to VM1, they are simultaneously conducting promotional activities for the ongoing construction of their micro foundry project. The representative mentioned, "Having secured specialized thin film manufacturing capabilities that meet various industry requirements, we are positively evaluating the potential for attracting customers." They added, "Especially considering the market demand for responsive semiconductors, we expect to achieve export results of over one million dollars in 2024."

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
